claim: to revert to the original mode, type this: printf '\033[0;37;40m\n'
quote: HOWTO: echo "^[[0;37;40m" to "revert back to the original mode". terminfo: sgr0 turns off all attribute modes; orig_pair (op) restores the original pair (example op=\E[39;49m). Forcing white-on-black SGR 0;37;40m is not a general original-mode restore.
earlier: matches — HOWTO itself presents that SGR string as the revert recipe

claim: control characters like suspend (CTRL-Z), interrupt and quit (CTRL-C)
quote: HOWTO groups "interrupt and quit (CTRL-C)". Man: cbreak leaves interrupt/quit/suspend unaffected (still signal); raw passes those characters through uninterpreted. Quit is not CTRL-C (typically CTRL-\\).
earlier: matches — those names are the control characters the HOWTO discusses for raw vs cbreak

claim: Other border functions draws lines with them (the forms-drawing characters)
quote: HOWTO §9.5: other border-related functions (mvhline/mvvline) create horizontal/vertical lines. curs_border: if chtype args are 0, curses uses forms-drawing characters.
earlier: can't tell — awkward "draws" wording without checking border man page for ACS defaults

claim: Initially the terminal has echoing enabled and is in ordinary cooked mode, so one or the other has to be changed before calling getch(); otherwise, the program's output will be unpredictable
quote: Intro: initially echoing enabled and cooked; one or the other has to [be] changed before getch(). curs_getch NOTES: wgetch with echo and neither cbreak nor raw is not well-defined.
earlier: matches — intro text alone already states the same rule

claim: While getnstr() is reading the line, F1 is ignored, like the other function keys
quote: wgetnstr: if (ch >= KEY_MIN || str-oldstr >= maxlen) beep; else store char. Man: discards function key inputs other than erase/kill synonyms, calling beep. KEY_F(1) is >= KEY_MIN, so it is rejected, not inserted.
earlier: can't tell — man page alone does not name F1 during getnstr

claim: Fifth is the color index. It is the index given during init_pair()
quote: chgat's pair argument is a color pair index (first argument of init_pair). curs_color uses "color index" for init_color palette entries, not for the chgat/init_pair pair number.
earlier: matches — HOWTO comment and chgat pair parameter both refer to init_pair's first argument

claim: Do this before the next wgetch(); otherwise another mouse event might come in and make the first one inaccessible
quote: Intro: must call getmouse before the next wgetch or another mouse event may make the first inaccessible. Man: getmouse removes the event from the queue after KEY_MOUSE; a subsequent getmouse retrieves the next older event.
earlier: matches — intro alone states the same warning

claim: An example showing all the characters, with 31 SHOW() lines and no ACS_URCORNER
quote: HOWTO: "Here is an example showing all the characters." Example has 31 SHOW("...") lines (ULCORNER/LLCORNER/LRCORNER present) and omits ACS_URCORNER, which curs_addch lists as a standard ACS symbol.
earlier: matches — counting SHOW lines already shows ACS_URCORNER is missing

claim: Note that new_field() does not copy the pointer array into private storage
quote: Intro says new_field() does not copy the pointer array, but the preceding text describes new_form(FIELD **). new_form stores the caller's array (form->field = fields); new_field creates one field and takes no pointer array.
earlier: matches — trusted the intro wording naming new_field()

claim: By default, all options are on.
quote: Man: standard field options are all on by default; extension options are off by default. default_field uses STD_FIELD_OPTS. Intro's "all options" accompanies the listed standard bits.
earlier: disagrees — extension options are off by default if "all" is read literally across every option bit

claim: Each field structure contains one character pointer slot ... The (char *) type is retained for System V compatibility
quote: Intro still documents char * userptr for System V compatibility. Current man page and form.h/fld_user.c use void * for set_field_userptr/field_userptr.
earlier: matches — intro alone still asserts the char* System V story

claim: The growth limit can be changed whether or not the O_STATIC bit is on, but has no effect until it is.
quote: set_max_field always assigns field->maxgrow; it only sets _MAY_GROW when O_STATIC is off. Man: set_max_field sets the maximum size for a dynamic field. Natural reading of "until it is" (O_STATIC on) is the opposite of when growth applies.
earlier: matches — accepted the intro sentence before comparing the pronoun to fld_max.c

claim: A REQ_MOVE_RIGHT from A will go to B
quote: Intro: REQ_MOVE_RIGHT from A goes to B only if A, B, and C all share the same first line; otherwise skips to C. API name is REQ_RIGHT_FIELD (REQ_MOVE_RIGHT is not defined). Right_Neighbor_Field cycles to the next field with the same frow.
earlier: disagrees — even the intro's next clause already qualifies "only if"

claim: the position of a form for purposes of these requests is its upper-left corner
quote: Intro inter-field navigation: "the position of a form for purposes of these requests is its upper-left corner." Neighbor helpers key off field->frow/fcol (field origin). No contradictory primary source found.
earlier: matches — accepted the intro sentence at face value

claim: REQ_DEL_PREV: Delete previous word at cursor.
quote: Intro list wrongly says "Delete previous word". Man: REQ_DEL_PREV = delete character before cursor; REQ_DEL_WORD = delete blank-delimited word. FE_Delete_Previous comment: "Delete character before cursor." Later intro prose also says previous character.
